Planned image-to-scute reader prototype (2026-10-18)

Current public API, behind feature image:
    trait Plan: Sized {
        fn plan(image: std::fs::File) -> io::Result<Self>;
    }
    impl Plan for Planned<std::fs::File>
    impl Read for Planned<std::fs::File>

With image + tokio:
    trait AsyncPlan: Sized {
        fn plan(image: tokio::fs::File)
            -> impl Future<Output = io::Result<Self>> + Send;
    }
    impl AsyncPlan for Planned<tokio::fs::File>
    impl AsyncRead for Planned<tokio::fs::File>

    impl<R> Planned<R> {
        fn exceptions(&self) -> u64;
        fn size(&self) -> u64;
    }

Import one construction trait, or use qualified syntax if both are in scope.
There is no Image wrapper, freestanding conversion function, conversion-result
struct, into_reader transition, or hash output. This
replaces the earlier sealed-file conversion prototype.

Construction is the first pass. It scans allocated extents in batches up to
1 MiB, skips sparse holes with SEEK_DATA/SEEK_HOLE, checks allocated chunks for
zeros, and generates all exception metadata. Memory retains 16 bytes per
exception plus metadata-area padding and container overhead. Source data is not
retained. Filesystems lacking sparse-query support fall back to scanning; they
may also conservatively expose holes as data without affecting correctness.

The resulting value is the reader for the second pass: it emits the header,
prepared metadata, and selected image chunks in COW order. Only selected chunks
are reread. A partial final image chunk is padded to 4096 bytes. No metadata-group
data buffer or output seeking is required. The async variant has a resumable
seek/read state machine and uses Tokio file I/O; only sparse queries are sent to
the blocking pool. Dropping construction does not leave a whole-file worker
running, though an already-dispatched file operation may finish.

Planned::size() returns the compact encoded length, including header,
data, and retained metadata chunks. An exactly full metadata area is followed
by an empty terminating area; the source size bound also bounds the output size. This is
not a size formula for arbitrary preexisting stores with holes/extra capacity.
Carapace uses fixed 4096-byte chunks. This known size lets callers configure the
existing verity formatter before consuming Planned. Tests compose the synchronous
reader through a tee to store COW bytes while hashing, and feed the async reader
directly to AsyncFormat. Verity's known-length contract is unchanged.

The source must remain immutable and exclusively used across BOTH passes,
including any duplicated descriptors. Construction requires a nonempty regular
file within the assembler's current 64 GiB dm-zero origin. Source I/O failures
propagate; after a read failure, subsequent nonempty reads fail. Caller storage,
publication, hashing, and persistence remain outside this API.

Snapshot wire API:
- Header::encode/decode, exceptions_per_chunk, metadata_chunk_index;
- Exception::encode/decode. Replay now uses decode to find selected source chunks.
The existing carapace assembly header reader also consumes Header::decode.

Validation:
- Both readers reconstruct fixtures at partial-block and metadata-area boundaries.
- Short/empty reads and repeat EOF, read failures, and async lazy construction.
- Dense and sparse representations produce identical bytes; blocking/async readers
  and existing verity formatters produce identical COW bytes/hash trees/roots.
- A 16 GiB sparse fixture with one nonzero and one allocated-zero chunk requires
  at most 1 MiB of planning reads and produces one exception in both paths.
- Output size checked against emitted bytes across metadata-area boundaries.
- Kernel dm-verity/snapshot assembly and readback passed using the planned reader
  streamed to a COW file and existing verity formatter together.
- Full carapace library tests, blocking-only image feature, default-disabled build,
  warnings-denied Clippy, formatting and diff checks run locally.

Cargo.toml pins devmap to committed revision 2679426fa1d4508fc5c3bbdf643efbdbe64a3edd;
no adjacent checkout or local dependency patches are required.
Conglobate and pichi consumers are not migrated; no remote CI run or commits are
part of this prototype. The separate bounded-memory, one-pass buffered converter
is not implemented by this planned-reader API.

Portability: conversion supports Linux, macOS, and Windows. Linux/macOS query
sparse extents; Windows queries allocated ranges through DeviceIoControl.
Device-mapper assembly and discovery remain Linux-only.
